description: This case study estimates what a Carrington-class solar storm would do to satellites in low Earth orbit with a spatiotemporal agent-based model in which each satellite is an agent that decides how to respond within propellant and collision avoidance limits. Rushil Kukreja, Edward Oughton, Phillip Cunio and Richard Linares posted it on arXiv in June 2026. The model draws on 41,644 satellite records, historical records of five recent space weather events and atmospheric density models. Scenario analysis suggests that 95% of LEO satellites would see drag about eight times baseline, raising collision risk two to three times, and Monte Carlo runs put direct economic impact near US$40 million per affected satellite; using real-time conditions, the model's manoeuvre advice was 92% accurate. Coverage is the global LEO population. Format and access: a preprint on arXiv. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free to read. Caveats: the model itself is not released, it is a prototype, and economic figures rest on assumptions about satellite value. It supports hazard exposure and resilience planning for space infrastructure and space traffic management. Related catalogue records are the pyatmos atmospheric density models and the CelesTrak satellite catalogue.
